value.text: The provided document is a summary of the United States Constitution . Its main points are: • [1] The Constitution creates a bicameral Congress with the House elected every two years and Senators appointed for six-year terms; the House holds sole impeachment trial power, while the Senate handles impeachments requiring a two-thirds majority. • [2] Bills must originate in the House before reaching the Senate, which can propose or concur with amendments. The President signs bills to make them law (or they take effect automatically unless Congress adjourns); if the President returns an objection within ten days, it requires a two-thirds vote in both houses to pass again. • [3] The President is elected for four years and serves as Commander in Chief; federal officers can be impeached only for high crimes and misdemeanors, and their salary remains fixed during their term. • [4] Treason is limited to levying war or aiding foreign enemies and requires two witnesses for conviction. The document mandates full faith and credit among states and protects each state's right to a republican form of government against invasion and domestic violence. • [5] The Constitution outlines the process for amending it via Congress (two-thirds proposal) or a convention called by two-thirds of state legislatures, requiring ratification from three-fourths of the states. It declares federal laws and treaties as supreme law over state judges and requires oaths from national leaders to support the Constitution. Summary of all 9 pages.
